context.full_target:
Theorem 1 (Logarithm-free convergence), with the standing definitions of Section 2 of the supplied paper.

Use normalized measure dx/(2*pi) on the torus \mathbb{T} = \mathbb{R}/(2*pi \mathbb{Z}). The Fourier coefficient is
\hat f(k)=(2*pi)^(-1) integral_0^(2*pi) f(x) exp(-i*k*x) dx,
and ||f||_(H^s)^2=sum_(k in Z) <k>^(2s)|\hat f(k)|^2, where <k>=(1+k^2)^(1/2).
These spaces are the completions of trigonometric polynomials in these norms; negative spaces are interpreted as distributions. The normalized L^2 norm is the s=0 norm. For mean-zero functions, the homogeneous norm uses |k|^(2s) in place of <k>^(2s). For s>=0,
||f||_(dot H^s)<=||f||_(H^s)<=2^(s/2)||f||_(dot H^s);
for s<0, 2^(s/2)||f||_(dot H^s)<=||f||_(H^s)<=||f||_(dot H^s).
Real-valued means \hat f(-k)=overline(\hat f(k)), and mean-zero means \hat f(0)=0.
All time suprema concern continuous representatives; derivative norms are essential suprema.

Let S_t=exp(-t*partial_x^3), so \widehat{S_t f}(k)=exp(i*t*k^3)\hat f(k).
Let P_0 be the mean and P=I-P_0. Let D^(-1)=partial_x^(-1) have multiplier (i*k)^(-1) for k!=0 and zero at k=0; D^(-2)=(D^(-1))^2.
The equation is
u_t+u_xxx=(1/2)partial_x(u^2),  u(0)=u_0. [Eq. (1)]
The exact solution u is the unique real, mean-zero C([0,T];H^gamma) solution obtained by smooth approximation and satisfies this equation distributionally.

For a positive integer L and tau=T/L, the fixed time-semidiscrete scheme is u^0=u_0 and
u^(n+1)=S_tau u^n+F_tau(u^n)+H_tau(u^n), 0<=n<L, [Eq. (2)]
where
F_tau(f)=(1/6)P[(S_tau D^(-1)f)^2]-(1/6)S_tau P[(D^(-1)f)^2],
H_tau(f)=(1/3)P[(S_tau D^(-1)f)D^(-1)F_tau(f)]
 +(tau/9)(S_tau D^(-1)f)P_0(f^2)
 -(1/54)[S_(tau-s)D^(-1)[(S_s D^(-1)f)^3]]_(s=0)^(s=tau)
 -(1/(27*tau))[S_(tau-s)D^(-2)[(S_(s-tau)D^(-2)F_tau(f))(S_s D^(-1)f)]]_(s=0)^(s=tau).
Each bracket [G(s)]_(s=0)^(s=tau) means G(tau)-G(0).
This is the fixed scheme of the paper's reference [1, Eq. (1.4)], without a spatial frequency cutoff.

For every T>0, every 0<gamma<=1 and every R>0, there exist C>0 and tau_0>0 depending only on T,gamma,R such that, for every real, mean-zero u_0 in H^gamma(\mathbb{T}) with ||u_0||_(H^gamma)<=R and every positive integer L with tau=T/L<=tau_0, this exact fixed scheme satisfies
max_(0<=n<=L) ||u(n*tau)-u^n||_(L^2)<=C*tau^gamma.
The same C and tau_0 apply to the entire stated initial-data ball; no spectral support bound or additional smoothness is a hypothesis.

In the source's standing notation v(t)=S_(-t)u(t) and M=1+sup_(0<=t<=T)||v(t)||_(H^gamma).
Constants C_M may vary from line to line and depend on gamma,T,M, but are uniform in n,tau and spectral support. Section 2.1 supplies M<=1+A(T,gamma,R) uniformly on the ball using the cited exact-flow results; it is not an extra hypothesis on u_0. The source uses the continuous estimates from [1, Proposition 3.4 and Lemma 7.2] and does not use the logarithmic convergence theorem as an input.
context.conclusion: There exist C>0 and tau_0>0 depending only on T,gamma,R such that, for every real mean-zero u_0 in H^gamma(Torus) with ||u_0||_(H^gamma)<=R and every positive integer Lsteps with tau=T/Lsteps<=tau_0, the exact solution of KdV(u;u_0) exists with the stipulated smooth-approximation meaning and the unfiltered recursion u^0=u_0, u^(n+1)=Psi_tau(u^n) satisfies max_(0<=n<=Lsteps)||u(n*tau)-u^n||_2<=C*tau^gamma. Both constants are uniform on the entire initial-data ball and independent of Fourier support and additional smoothness.

record.definition: Torus=ℝ/(2*pi*ℤ), with measure dx/(2*pi) on [0,2*pi). Here ℝ denotes the real number system, distinct from the radius parameter R.
For a periodic integrable f and k in Z, Fourier(f)(k)=(2*pi)^(-1) integral_0^(2*pi) f(x) exp(-i*k*x) dx; write hat f(k). Extend by completion and distribution duality.

For real s, H^s(Torus) is the completion of trigonometric polynomials for ||f||_(H^s)^2=sum_(k in Z)(1+k^2)^s |hat f(k)|^2. Negative spaces are periodic distributions. L^2=H^0 with the normalized measure. Real means hat f(-k)=overline(hat f(k)); mean-zero means hat f(0)=0. Write ||.||_2 for ||.||_(L^2).

record.type: homogeneous Sobolev norms on the mean-zero subspaces

record.definition: S_t=exp(-t*partial_x^3), hat(S_t f)(k)=exp(i*t*k^3)*hat f(k). Thus S_(t+r)=S_t S_r, S_0=I and each S_t is an isometry on every H^s by its unit-modulus multiplier.
P0 f=hat f(0), the mean, identified with a constant function.
P=I-P0.
Dinv=partial_x^(-1); hat(Dinv f)(k)=(i*k)^(-1)hat f(k) for k!=0 and zero for k=0. Dinv2=(Dinv)^2=partial_x^(-2). These formulas define maps H^s -> H^(s+1) and H^s -> H^(s+2), respectively.
For tau>0 and mean-zero f in L^2, Ftau(f)=(1/6)P[(S_tau Dinv f)^2]-(1/6)S_tau P[(Dinv f)^2].

H_tau(f)=(1/3)P[(S_tau D^(-1)f)D^(-1)F_tau(f)]
 +(tau/9)(S_tau D^(-1)f)P_0(f^2)
 -(1/54)[S_(tau-s)D^(-1)[(S_s D^(-1)f)^3]]_(s=0)^(s=tau)
 -(1/(27*tau))[S_(tau-s)D^(-2)[(S_(s-tau)D^(-2)F_tau(f))(S_s D^(-1)f)]]_(s=0)^(s=tau).
Each bracket [G(s)]_(s=0)^(s=tau) means G(tau)-G(0).
Notation in this copied formula: H_tau=Htau at timestep tau, F_tau=Ftau, P_0=P0, D^(-1)=Dinv and D^(-2)=(Dinv)^2=Dinv2; S_r is the group S at time r. The bracket variable G denotes the entire expression depending on s inside that bracket.

record.type: unmodified time-step map and finite numerical trajectories
record.definition: Psi_tau(f)=S_tau f+Ftau(f)+Htau(f), tau>0. For a positive integer Lsteps and tau=T/Lsteps>0, set t_n=n*tau and u^0=u_0, u^(n+1)=Psi_tau(u^n), 0<=n<Lsteps; v^n=S_(-t_n)u^n. No spatial frequency cutoff is applied. This is a finite recursion; its L^2 continuity and preservation properties are proved below.
Ple_N f has coefficients 1_(|k|<=N)*hat f(k), N>=0; Pgt_N=I-Ple_N. These are used only in the proof and in initial-data approximation.
Mavg_tau g=(1/tau) integral_0^tau g(s) ds, tau>0.

record.type: average covariance of two exponential phases
record.definition:
For real alpha,beta,
M_tau g=(1/tau) integral_0^tau g(s) ds,
eta_tau(alpha,beta)=M_tau(exp(-i*s*(alpha+beta)))-M_tau(exp(-i*s*alpha))*M_tau(exp(-i*s*beta)).
The notation M_tau here means Mavg_tau; eta_tau is the family eta at timestep tau.

record.type: smooth-input trilinear averaged cubic remainder with a polynomial dense core
record.definition: For tau>0,t0>=0 and mean-zero trigonometric polynomials f_1,f_2,f_3, define hat(Rem_(t0,tau)(f_1,f_2,f_3))(k)=-tau/(18*i*k) sum_(a+b+c=k,a+b!=0) exp(-i*t0*Phi)*eta_tau(alpha,beta)*hat f_1(a)*hat f_2(b)*hat f_3(c) for k!=0, and zero at k=0. Here p=a+b, alpha=3*a*b*p, beta=3*k*c*p, Phi=alpha+beta=k^3-a^3-b^3-c^3. The notation R^n_(2,tau) means Rem_(n*tau,tau). The extension to Sobolev inputs is a proved conclusion below, not an assumed estimate. The same Fourier formula defines the operator for smooth inputs by absolutely convergent series: |eta|<=2 from the two averages and smooth Fourier coefficients are rapidly decreasing, so the triple sum is absolutely convergent. The polynomial restriction is its initial dense core.
pstar=23/14.

For an interval I with length at most one, X(I) consists of L^infinity(I;L^2) functions with weak time derivative in L^infinity(I;H^(-pstar)); ||f||_(X(I))=||f||_(L^infinity(I;L^2))+||f'||_(L^infinity(I;H^(-pstar))). All time suprema of continuous functions use their continuous representatives; derivatives and L^infinity norms use essential suprema.
B_t(f,g)=S_(-t) partial_x[(S_t f)(S_t g)], initially for smooth periodic inputs, and in H^(-pstar) for L^2 inputs by the bound proved below.
J_t(f,g)=S_(-t)P[(S_t Dinv f)(S_t Dinv g)].

Ctri_I(f,g,h)=integral_I S_(-t)P{P[(S_t f(t))(S_t g(t))]*(S_t Dinv h(t))} dt. For time-independent inputs suppress their t dependence. Initially use smooth spatial inputs, with piecewise smooth continuous time dependence; bounded extensions are justified by the explicit sources or estimates below.
Fstage_(a,t)(f,g)=(1/2) integral_a^t B_s(f,g) ds for time-independent smooth mean-zero f,g and a<=t. Fstage_(a,t)(f) abbreviates Fstage_(a,t)(f,f).

For a>=0,tau>0 and smooth mean-zero f, on [a,a+tau] put F(t)=Fstage_(a,t)(f), z(t)=f+F(t), Cst(t)=integral_a^t B_s(f,F(s)) ds, Q(t)=(1/2)integral_a^t B_s(F(s),F(s)) ds, W=Q(a+tau)+Rem_(a,tau)(f,f,f), Vst(t)=f+F(t)+Cst(t)+Q(t)-((t-a)/tau)*W, Y(t)=Vst(t)-z(t). Interp_(a,tau;f) denotes this entire tuple (F,z,Cst,Q,W,Vst,Y). It is just these formulas, with no error estimates or endpoint matching granted.

KdV(u;u_0) means u_t+u_xxx=(1/2)partial_x(u^2), u(0)=u_0 on Torus, distributionally. The exact solution sought for real mean-zero u_0 in H^gamma is the unique real mean-zero C([0,T];H^gamma) solution obtained by smooth approximation. This predicate itself asserts no existence or quantitative bound.

record.statement: For the real mean-zero periodic equation U_t=U*U_x+U_xxx on ℝ/(2*pi*ℤ), use hat U(k)=(2*pi)^(-1) integral U(x)exp(-i*k*x)dx, ||U||_(dot H^s)^2=sum_(k!=0)|k|^(2s)|hat U(k)|^2, and z_k(t)=exp(i*k^3*t)hat U(t)(k). For every s>0 and horizon Q>0, every initial datum U_0 in dot H^s has a distributional solution with z in C([0,Q];dot H^s), unique in the source solution class (z in L^infinity dot H^0 satisfying z_k(t)-z_k(0)=(i*k/2)integral_0^t sum_(k1+k2=k)exp(i*3*k*k1*k2*r)z_k1(r)z_k2(r)dr). Its dot H^0 norm is conserved, and the flow depends Lipschitz continuously on the initial data in dot H^s, uniformly on bounded dot H^s sets on [0,Q]. The Galerkin approximations (with the nonlinear inputs and output projected to |k|<=m and high coefficients frozen) have dot H^s bounds uniform in m, depending only on s,Q, the initial dot H^s norm and an upper bound for the initial dot H^0 norm. For 0<sigma<s they admit a subsequence converging strongly in L^q([0,Q];dot H^sigma), 1<q<infinity, and weak-* in L^infinity dot H^s to this solution; the same dot H^s bound holds for the limit. For s=0 there is a unique C([0,Q];dot H^0) solution, conserving that norm and depending Lipschitz continuously on its data. These flows agree on overlapping regularity classes and are obtained by smooth approximation.

source.author: Anatoli V. Babin; Alexei A. Ilyin; Edriss S. Titi
source.title: On the regularization mechanism for the periodic Korteweg-de Vries equation
hypotheses: The torus has length 2*pi, the datum is real and mean-zero.
The horizon Q is positive and the nonnegative Sobolev regularity and initial norms are as stated.
source.context: Source Sections 3-4 specify the homogeneous normalized norms and the coefficient solution notion. Theorem 4.2 gives uniform Galerkin bounds, 4.3 the limiting solution for positive s, 5.1 uniqueness and continuity for s>1/2, 6.3 for 0<s<=1/2, 6.4 for s=0. Uniformity on norm-bounded sets is the quantitative content of the estimates in their proofs, not a new hypothesis.
source.source_statement: Imported exact-flow clauses of the cited theorem suite: Theorem 4.2: if v^(m)(0)=v0 in dot H^s0, s0>=0, ||v^(m)(0)||_(dot H^0)<=M0 and T>0, then ||v^(m)(t)||_(dot H^s0)<=M_s0 on [0,T], uniformly in m, where M_s0 depends only on M0,T,||v0||_(dot H^s0),s0. Theorem 4.3: for s0>0, v0 in dot H^s0,T>0,0<sigma<s0, a subsequence converges strongly in L^p([0,T];H^sigma), 1<p<infinity, and weak-* in L^infinity dot H^s0 to a solution of (3.8) in Definition 3.1, bounded by M_s0, with dot H^0 norm equal to its initial norm a.e. Theorem 5.1: for s>1/2 that solution is unique, C([0,T];dot H^s), Lipschitz in initial data as in (5.18), and conserves dot H^0 for all t. Theorem 6.3: for 0<s<=1/2 it is unique, C([0,T];dot H^s), and Lipschitz as in (6.7). Theorem 6.4: for s=0 there is a unique C([0,T];dot H^0) solution depending Lipschitz continuously on its data. Section 3 identifies these coefficient solutions with the physical U_t=UU_x+U_xxx; the proofs construct them by Galerkin or smooth limits.
source.notation_map: The source physical field is called U here; source twisted coefficients are z_k=exp(i*k^3*t)*hat U(k). Its normalized homogeneous Sobolev norms agree with Hdot. The reflection/sign bridge to our KdV is proved in N001.

record.statement: For Q>0, theta in (-1,0] and real mean-zero initial data U_0,W_0 in dot H^0 with ||U_0||_(dot H^0)+||W_0||_(dot H^0)<=B0, the two source twisted solutions z,y of z_k'=(i*k/2)sum_(k1+k2=k) exp(i*3*k*k1*k2*t)z_k1*z_k2 with these initial coefficients satisfy sup_(0<=t<=Q)||z(t)-y(t)||_(dot H^theta)<=C'(B0,theta)*C_(B0,theta)^Q*||U_0-W_0||_(dot H^theta). record.statement: For tau>0, n>=0 integer, t_n=n*tau and a smooth real mean-zero f, let uold=S_(t_n)f and unew=Psi_tau(uold), with the displayed unfiltered update. Then S_(-(t_n+tau))unew=f+Fstage_(t_n,t_n+tau)(f)+integral_(t_n)^(t_n+tau) B_s(f,Fstage_(t_n,s)(f)) ds-Rem_(t_n,tau)(f,f,f). source.context: Source A^n[f] is the integral B(f,Fstage); H^n=A^n-R_2^n by (4.20). Equation (4.23) identifies its physical scheme with (1.4). The phase and remainder of (4.15),(4.17),(6.1) match D014-D015; the spurious trailing ds in the printed (4.17) is absent in (6.1).
source.source_statement: The source identities are: A^n[f]=H^n[f]+R_2^n[f] (4.20); v^(n+1)=v^n+F^n[t_(n+1);v^n]+H^n[v^n] (4.22); u^(n+1)=exp(-tau*partial_x^3)u^n+exp(-t_(n+1)*partial_x^3)F^n[t_(n+1);exp(t_n*partial_x^3)u^n]+exp(-t_(n+1)*partial_x^3)H^n[exp(t_n*partial_x^3)u^n] (4.23), equal to (1.4). Thus (5.2) states v^(n+1)=v^n+F^n[t_(n+1);v^n]+A^n[v^n]-R_2^n[v^n]. F^n=(1/2)integral B, A^n=integral B(f,F^n). The nonzero Fourier coefficient of R_2^n is -tau/(18*i*k)sum_(a+b+c=k,a+b!=0)exp(-i*t_n*Phi)*eta*hat f(a)hat f(b)hat f(c), with eta=M_tau(exp(-is(phi1+phi2)))-M_tau(exp(-is phi1))*M_tau(exp(-is phi2)), phi1=3ab(a+b), phi2=3kc(a+b).

record.statement: There is A=A(T,gamma,R)<infinity such that every real mean-zero datum a0 in H^gamma(Torus) with ||a0||_(H^gamma)<=R has a unique real mean-zero exact KdV solution u in C([0,T];H^gamma), obtained by smooth approximation, satisfying sup_[0,T]||u(t)||_(H^gamma)<=A. Smooth data have smooth solutions. If a0,b0 are two such data then sup_[0,T]||u_a0(t)-u_b0(t)||_2<=K(T,2*R)||a0-b0||_2. The same estimate holds for any two real mean-zero L^2 data with sum of norms <=2*R. Twisting v(t)=S_(-t)u(t) preserves these bounds; for smooth data v'=(1/2)B_t(v,v). Thus M=1+sup_[0,T]||v(t)||_(H^gamma)<=1+A uniformly on the original ball.

For nonzero integers a,b,c,d with a+b+c+d=0, let N1>=N2>=N3>=N4 be the rearranged magnitudes and A0=|a*b|,B0=|c*d|. Then N1<=3*N2, (1/|d|)min(A0/B0,B0/A0)<=3/N3 and |a+b|/max(A0,B0)<=6/N3. Moreover for any nonnegative x_1,x_2,x_3,x_4 in ell^2(Z\{0}), sum_(a+b+c+d=0,abcd!=0) product_(j=1)^4 x_j(k_j)/N3(a,b,c,d)<=C*product_j||x_j||_(ell^2), where (k_1,k_2,k_3,k_4)=(a,b,c,d), and C is absolute. The same bound holds on any subset of these interactions, and the infinite positive sum is the supremum of its finite restrictions.

record.statement: For every 0<=sigma<=1, tau>0, t0>=0 and mean-zero f_j in H^sigma, Rem_(t0,tau) has a unique bounded trilinear extension with ||Rem_(t0,tau)(f_1,f_2,f_3)||_2<=C_sigma*tau^(1+sigma)*product_j||f_j||_(H^sigma), uniformly in t0,tau and Fourier support. In the nonzero interaction a+b+c=k, d=-k, the multiplier obeys |eta_tau(3ab(a+b),3kc(a+b))|/(|k||abc|^sigma)<=6^(1-sigma)*18^sigma*tau^sigma/N3(a,b,c,-k). The same estimates hold with any additional interaction multiplier of modulus <=1, including restrictions to Phi=0 or Phi!=0. In particular if 0<sigma<=1, 0<tau<=1, w in mean-zero H^sigma, f in mean-zero L^2, ||w||_(H^sigma)<=M0 and delta=||f-w||_2<=1, then ||Rem_(t0,tau)(f,f,f)||_2<=C_(sigma,M0)*tau*(tau^sigma+delta), with no Sobolev hypothesis on f.

record.statement: For each fixed tau>0, Psi_tau is a continuous map on the real mean-zero L^2 space, preserves mean zero and reality, and maps smooth data to smooth data; Ftau:L^2->H^1 is continuous. Hence all finite numerical trajectories are defined and continuous in the initial datum. For every smooth mean-zero real f, tau>0 and integer n>=0, S_(-(n+1)*tau)Psi_tau(S_(n*tau)f)=f+Fstage_(n*tau,(n+1)*tau)(f)+integral_(n*tau)^((n+1)*tau)B_s(f,Fstage_(n*tau,s)(f))ds-Rem_(n*tau,tau)(f,f,f). Consequently on a numerical smooth trajectory the tuple Interp_(t_n,tau;v^n) has Vst(t_n)=v^n and Vst(t_(n+1))=v^(n+1). The interpolants therefore concatenate to a continuous piecewise smooth mean-zero real V on [0,T].

If I=[a,b] starts at a grid point, h=b-a<=1, e=v-V and E_I=sup_I||e||_2<=1, including an endpoint inside a step, one has sup_(t in I)||Rres(t)-Rres(a)||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*(h+tau)*(tau^gamma+E_I), ||e||_(X(I))<=C_(gamma,M0)*(tau^gamma+E_I), and ||v||_(X(I))+||V||_(X(I))<=C_(gamma,M0). record.statement: Fix 0<gamma<=1 and M0>=1. There exist delta0 in (0,1] and K0>0, depending only on gamma,M0, with the following property. For any 0<tau<=delta0/2, any smooth real mean-zero exact twisted path v satisfying v'=(1/2)B_t(v,v), sup||v||_(H^gamma)<=M0, and any smooth real mean-zero numerical trajectory with interpolation V obtained from Interp at its grid values, let e=v-V. On every interval I=[a,b] starting at a grid point, with h=b-a<=delta0 and E_I=sup_I||e||_2<=1, one has E_I<=2||e(a)||_2+K0*delta0*tau^gamma. The endpoint b may lie inside a step. More precisely the proof gives for all N>=2,h<=1,0<tau<=1 under this bootstrap: e(t)=e(a)+F_I(t)-(Rres(t)-Rres(a)), F_I(t)=integral_a^t B_s(e,v-e/2)ds; sup_I||Ple_N F_I||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*N^2*h*E_I; F_I=(1/3)[J_s(e,v-e/2)]_a^t-(1/3)Ctri_[a,t](e,v-e/2,V)-(1/6)Ctri_[a,t](v,v,e)+(1/3)integral_a^t J_s(Rres',V)ds; sup_I||Pgt_N F_I||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*(h+tau)*tau^gamma+C_(gamma,M0)*(h+tau+N^(-1)+N^(-pstar))*E_I; and E_I<=||e(a)||_2+C_(gamma,M0)*(h+tau)*tau^gamma+C_(gamma,M0)*(N^2*h+h+tau+N^(-1)+N^(-pstar))*E_I. Here Rres is the concatenation of the step increments rho_n(t)=-integral_(t_n)^t B_s(Y_n,z_n)ds-(1/2)integral_(t_n)^t B_s(Y_n,Y_n)ds-((t-t_n)/tau)W_n, where the subscripted tuple is Interp_(t_n,tau;v^n), with Rres(0)=0, and every constant is independent of time index, timestep, spectral support and higher norms.
